account.credentialsRequired: Enter a username and a password.
account.loginRequired: Enter a username and a password.
account.passwordTooShort: The password needs at least {{min}} characters and several character classes.
accountDialog.passwordHint: At least 12 characters; submitted to the backend which stores only the hash, never saved or echoed on this page.
accountDialog.subtitle: Set the initial password on creation; the server only stores the password hash and the page never echoes credentials.
accountDialog.title: Add account
accounts.intro.description: Maintain sign-in identities, status and role entry points. Passwords are only kept on the server; this page never displays or echoes credentials.
accounts.intro.title: Account maintenance
accounts.notice.created: The account was added to the demo list; a real environment creates and audits it through a backend API.
accounts.notice.statusChanged: The status change only affects the current demo page and was not written to the server.
accounts.panel.subtitle: The built-in administrator cannot be deleted; disabling an account immediately rejects new sign-in requests.
accounts.panel.title: Account list
changePassword.field.nextHint: At least 12 characters; do not reuse the account name or an environment name.
changePassword.intro.description: Set a new sign-in password for account {{username}}. The password is only submitted to the backend for validation and never enters the URL, logs or browser storage.
changePassword.intro.title: Change password
changePassword.panel.subtitle: Use a password manager to generate a unique password; after the change other sessions can be invalidated.
changePassword.panel.title: Update sign-in password
changePassword.success: Demo validation passed; a real environment calls the change-password API and never stores the password on the page.
login.description: After signing in you can review instance status, traffic trends and rule versions. Demo accounts: admin (view metrics and edit rules), viewer (read-only).
login.title: Sign in to the console
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
password.tooShort: The new password needs at least {{min}} characters and several character classes.
roles.accountPanel.subtitle: An account is bound to exactly one role at a time, which avoids ambiguity from permission combinations.
roles.accountPanel.title: Select an account
roles.bindingPanel.subtitle: After the change the backend must record the operator, the reason and the effective time.
roles.bindingPanel.title: Bind a role
roles.intro.description: Roles are the only authorization entry point: admin can maintain rules, view can only read metrics and events.
roles.intro.title: Role binding
roles.role.admin.description: View all runtime data, and create, modify, publish and roll back flow-control rules.
roles.role.admin.title: Administrator
roles.role.view.description: View the overview, instances, monitoring and incident analysis; no editing capability at all.
roles.role.view.title: Viewer
roles.warning: The front-end selection only changes demo state; the server must re-validate permissions on every request.
setup.adminPasswordMismatch: The two administrator passwords do not match.
setup.adminRequired: Enter the administrator details and set a password of at least {{min}} characters.
setup.credentialReferenceHint: Enter a reference from a secret manager, Kubernetes Secret or deployment config; do not enter passwords, tokens or private keys.
setup.credentialReferenceRequired: Enter a deployment credential reference, or choose to enter credentials directly / disable authentication.
setup.directNote: For controlled intranets. Credentials are submitted write-only to the backend over TLS; the browser never stores, echoes or re-reads them.
setup.info.connectionTested: Demo connection check passed; a real service establishes the connection, runs migrations and returns a requestId.
setup.intro.description: First establish this system's persistence foundation, then create the built-in administrator and register the rule config center.
setup.intro.title: Initialize the control plane
setup.nacosCredentialsRequired: Enter the Nacos username and password.
setup.noneNote: {{source}} will be connected anonymously. Use this only when network isolation, access control and TLS are already guaranteed by the deployment environment.
setup.option.consul.description: Like Nacos, an authoritative rule source; not used for account or audit storage.
setup.option.credentialReference.descrip: A secret manager, Kubernetes Secret or deployment config provides the credentials to the server.
setup.option.credentialReference.label: Use a deployment credential reference
setup.option.direct.description: For controlled intranets; credentials are submitted write-only to the backend and never shown on the page again.
setup.option.direct.label: Enter credentials in the console
setup.option.mysql.description: Production ready, requires MySQL 8.0+; MariaDB must be evaluated as a separate compatibility item.
setup.option.nacos.description: The management service publishes complete rule snapshots through a controlled write-back flow.
setup.option.none.description: Only for config centers that are isolated and explicitly allow anonymous access; TLS is still recommended.
setup.option.none.label: Disable authentication
setup.option.postgres.description: Production ready, for reliable control-plane persistence.
setup.option.sqlite.description: Local experience or single-machine development only; not for production cluster storage.
setup.sqliteNote: The SQLite data file is stored in the server's controlled data directory; the browser never stores database content.
setup.stage.admin.description: This account is the first admin; the system does not generate, display or retain any default password.
setup.stage.admin.title: Create the built-in administrator
setup.stage.database.description: Accounts, roles, audit, drafts, rule versions and release plans need a relational database; active rules are still not written to it directly.
setup.stage.database.title: Configure the system database
setup.stage.finish.description: When finished, the system records the initialization state, creates the built-in administrator and opens sign-in and the console API.
setup.stage.finish.title: Confirm and finish
setup.stage.source.description: Choose the first rule source for this deployment; another source can be added later under system management.
setup.stage.source.title: Register the rule config center
setup.step.admin.description: Create the single first admin; the system provides no default password.
setup.step.admin.label: Built-in administrator
setup.step.database.description: Verify the database connection and create the control-plane schema.
setup.step.database.label: System storage
setup.step.finish.description: Record the initialization result and open sign-in and the console API.
setup.step.finish.label: Finish initialization
setup.step.source.description: Register Nacos or Consul; rules remain authoritatively held by the config center.
setup.step.source.label: Rule source
setup.warning: Initialization is a one-time protected operation. Production must supply a bootstrap key or a managed secret; the server must never store the database password as a plaintext file.
